technology.summary: Today's technology news includes the announcement of Microsoft's new AI chip, the Maia 300, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. Amazon has over one million robot workers, which raises questions about the future of human employees. TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will focus on building enduring companies in the AI era. Other news includes the launch of the Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker, and the upcoming Apple "Welcome Home" event, which will feature smart home-related announcements.

finance.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have teamed up to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. A resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt. The Supreme Court of India has also highlighted troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals, urging a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications.

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence, and the Supreme Court's decision to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar. Congress has claimed that tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai were detained, and the CEC's ability to execute illegal orders has been criticised. Meanwhile, former US President Donald Trump has cited a non-existent Indian election to call the US electoral process 'corrupt', and India's foreign exchange reserves have reportedly declined by USD 18.34 billion in a single week.
